Core: dot→(q,r)→CSD→shift→latch-acc ─drain→ {softmax→p_fifo→PV} | {normalize→1/l→FP16}

Phân vùng bank sạch (Q=bank16, K/V=bank0..15, OUT=bank17), không đụng nhau — tốt. Crossbar fixed-priority cho streamer thắng DMA — đúng ý đồ. Toàn bộ khớp bit-exact 1024/1024, 1024/1024, 2048/2048.

① QK bị tính lại theo từng DV-slice — lãng phí lớn nhất

Vòng lặp là h → qi → dvi → kj (theo đúng comment) nên QK được tính lại DV_TILES lần cho cùng (h,qi) dù P = softmax(QK) không phụ thuộc dvi.

  • tb_llama: DV_TILES=8 → QK lặp 8× ⇒ 4608 vs 1024 beat (giảm ~4.5×). Đây là với shape LLaMA thật.

Cách sửa: cache P của cả group (chỉ ~KV_TILES×M_Q gói 72b ≈ 288 B) vào TCDM hoặc một P-buffer đủ lớn, rồi đảo vòng lặp kj → dvi để dùng lại P; hoặc giữ nhiều O-accumulator hơn (tăng ACC_DEPTH). Đây là tối ưu kiến trúc, đáng làm nhất.

② O-drain / đường ra bị tuần tự hoá (5 cyc/slot)

  • Write-out FP16 ghi 4 word vào cùng bank 17 (line_stride = 0x200 = word+1), mỗi chu kỳ 1 word → 4–5 cyc/vector; core chỉ có 1 output hold register nên drain bị chặn.
  • out_fifo_ready_o bị tie 1'b1 (stub) nên core_out_fifo_ready_i trong sequencer vô nghĩa.

Cách sửa: thêm output FIFO thật (8 entry) giữa normalizer và write-out, và stripe 4 word FP16 ra 4 bank khác nhau để ghi song song. Cần sửa đúng bug "vector cuối" đã từng gặp (comment ghi đã revert).

③ Serialize O-drain với QK kế tiếp vì dùng chung l

Đây chính là nguyên nhân ② cộng dồn: phải đợi O-drain xong vì softmax group sau ghi đè l/inv_l của cùng bộ query. Double-buffer l/reciprocal (hoặc index thêm theo dvi) sẽ cho O-drain chạy song song QK group sau, xoá ~144 cyc dôi ra.

Hiện depth=16, MQ=8 nên chưa lộ, nhưng là lỗi tiềm ẩn (ví dụ tăng MQ hoặc giảm depth). Nên thêm && !p_fifo_almost_full_i vào điều kiện drain S.

⑤ Vài điểm nhỏ

  • Packet 72-bit = 9 byte: không power-of-2, DMA/burst/align kém. Cân nhắc 128-bit có padding hoặc tách "scale plane" 8-bit riêng.
  • Interconnect giữ 1 read in-flight/bank (read_in_flight_q 1 bit): đúng khi SRAM latency = 1 cyc, nhưng sẽ sai nếu bank thành pipelined/multi-cycle. Nên ghi chú ràng buộc.
  • Output hold register: packed = hold ? hold : src — nếu out_ready=0 và có vector mới từ normalizer thì vector mới bị bỏ. Hiện may mắn không xảy ra do pacing 5 cyc, nhưng rất mong manh → FIFO ② sẽ khử luôn.
  • snax_llm_top.sv: địa chỉ hard-code (0x1000, 0x2000) — không dùng được, nên xoá/đánh dấu rõ để tránh nhầm với top thật.
  • PV 80%: có thể nâng nhẹ bằng cách prefetch/khởi động PV sớm 1–2 cyc để p_fifo kịp đầy.

Data flow hợp lý và đã verify bit-exact; kiến trúc FP4 log-scale + latch-accumulator + exp-free softmax là nhất quán. Nếu chỉ xét "đúng", không có lỗi. Còn nếu tối ưu, thứ tự nên làm:

Let me verify by re-reading the relevant sequencer loop progression to be accurate. I already have the code. Let me re-derive carefully.

Loop counters: cnt_h, cnt_qi, cnt_dvi, cnt_kj. Progression happens in ST_ATTN_PV_DRAIN when last kv tile of group: on cnt_kj wrap, advance dvi; if dvi last, advance qi; if qi last, advance h. And QK_LAUNCH is entered per kv tile.

The attention math:
- Q: [N_Q, D_K], K: [N_KV, D_K], V: [N_KV, D_V]
- S = Q·K^T : [N_Q, N_KV]
- P = softmax(S) : [N_Q, N_KV]
- O = P·V : [N_Q, D_V]

O has D_V columns. The hardware processes D_V in slices of 16 (DV_TILES = D_V/16). So O is computed per dvi slice: O[:, dvi*16:(dvi+1)*16] = P · V[:, dvi*16:...].

P is shared across all dvi slices. So you compute P (which requires S = Q·K^T over full D_K, all N_KV) once, then reuse for each dvi.

Current loop: for h, for qi (query tile of M_Q=8), for dvi, for kj (KV tile):
  - QK: for each kj, compute S block = Q_tile · K[kj]^T  (M_Q x 16 scores)
  - softmax → P block
  - PV: for each kj, O_tile += P_block · V[kj, dvi]
So for fixed (h, qi), the loop over dvi repeats the ENTIRE QK over all kj, and the softmax, DV_TILES times. Only the V operand changes (V[kj, dvi]).

Why is it done this way? Because O accumulator storage: 8 O slots (M_Q=8 queries) in the 16-slot latch array (8 for S, 8 for O). If they looped dvi inner (kj outer), they'd need to keep O for all dvi slices simultaneously = DV_TILES × M_Q slots, which doesn't fit. So they put dvi outer and recompute.

Concrete example for the clean TB:
- H=2, N_Q=16 (Q_TILES=2, M_Q=8), N_KV=32 (KV_TILES=2), D_K=32 (K_BLOCKS=2), D_V=32 (DV_TILES=2).
- Current QK beats = H × Q_TILES × DV_TILES × KV_TILES × M_Q × K_BLOCKS = 2×2×2×2×8×2 = 256. ✓ matches qk_fire=256.
- If QK computed once per (h, qi, kj) and reused across dvi: = 2×2×2×8×2 = 128. So half. (DV_TILES=2 factor).
- PV beats (unchanged) = H × Q_TILES × DV_TILES × KV_TILES × M_Q = 2×2×2×2×8 = 128. ✓ pv_fire=128.
- Total 384 → 256 = 33% reduction.

For LLaMA TB: H=1, Q_TILES=2, DV_TILES=8, KV_TILES=4, M_Q=8, K_BLOCKS=8.
- QK beats current = 1×2×8×4×8×8 = 4096.
- Optimal = 1×2×4×8×8 = 512 (8× less).
- PV = 1×2×8×4×8 = 512.
- Total 4608 → 1024 = 4.5× less.

So the redundancy factor is exactly DV_TILES. The QK work is proportional to DV_TILES but the information (P) doesn't depend on dvi.

Note also the softmax work is recomputed DV_TILES times (though softmax is cheap-ish). And K is re-read from TCDM DV_TILES times (bandwidth waste), and Q too.

Now explain "why it's wasteful" and "how to fix": cache P. P for a group = N_KV × M_Q values; as FP4 packets: KV_TILES × M_Q packets of 72 bits = for LLaMA 4×8=32 packets × 9B = 288 B. Tiny. Store P to TCDM, then loop dvi: for each dvi, for each kj, load P block (no QK), multiply by V[kj,dvi], accumulate into O[queries] (one dvi at a time → fits 8 slots). This keeps O storage requirement the same (8 slots) while eliminating QK redundancy!

Wait — if we loop dvi outer and load cached P, we still only need 8 O slots per dvi. So the fix is: Phase 1 for group (h,qi): compute QK once over all kj, softmax, and STORE P blocks to TCDM (instead of only p_fifo). Phase 2: for each dvi, stream V[kj,dvi] and cached P[kj] (re-read from TCDM), accumulate O, drain. This preserves the 16-slot accumulator and removes DV_TILES-1 redundant QK passes.

Actually even simpler: keep P in an on-chip P buffer sized KV_TILES×M_Q (or a full N_KV×M_Q). For LLaMA that's 32×72b = 2.3 Kbit, trivial. Then no TCDM round trip.

Alternatively reorder loop nest to kj outer / dvi inner requires all dvi O accumulators simultaneously → needs DV_TILES×M_Q slots (LLaMA 64 slots) → bigger latch array. So caching P is preferable given current accumulator size.

Toán học

Attention với một head:

S = Q · Kᵀ          [N_Q × N_KV]      ← cần tính
P = softmax(S)      [N_Q × N_KV]      ← không phụ thuộc D_V
O = P · V           [N_Q × D_V]       ← D_V được chia thành DV_TILES slice 16 cột

Kết quả O được tính từng slice 16 cột của V: O[:, dvi] = P · V[:, dvi]. Nhưng P giống nhau cho mọi dvi — nó chỉ phụ thuộc Q và K. Vì vậy S và softmax đúng ra chỉ cần tính một lần cho mỗi (h, qi), rồi dùng lại cho tất cả slice V.

Nhưng sequencer đang làm ngược lại

Vòng lặp trong snax_llm_sequencer là 4 tầng: h → qi → dvi → kj (đúng như comment đầu file):

for h:
  for qi:                 // Q-tile, M_Q=8 query
    for dvi:              // DV-slice (16 cột của V)
      for kj:             // KV-tile
         QK: S = Q_tile · K[kj]ᵀ        ← tính lại từ đầu
         softmax → P block
         PV: O[dvi] += P · V[kj, dvi]

Bằng chứng trong code — counter chỉ nhảy dvi sau khi xong toàn bộ kj, rồi FSM quay lại ST_ATTN_QK_LAUNCH (chạy lại QK cho mọi kj ở dvi mới):

// ST_ATTN_PV_DRAIN → khi hết kj:
if (cnt_kj_q == 0)                 // vừa wrap sau kv-tile cuối
    state_d = last_group_q ? ST_ATTN_LAST_DRAIN : ST_ATTN_QK_LAUNCH;

// cập nhật counter (PV_RUN, beat cuối):
if (cnt_dvi_q == DV_TILES-1) begin cnt_dvi_q <= 0; ... end
else cnt_dvi_q <= cnt_dvi_q + 1;   // dvi tăng → QK chạy lại

Nên với cùng (h, qi), toàn bộ QK + softmax bị lặp đúng DV_TILES lần, chỉ có toán hạng V là đổi. K và Q cũng bị đọc lại từ TCDM DV_TILES lần.

Vì sao tác giả làm vậy?

Vì bộ tích lũy O chỉ có 8 slot (ACC_DEPTH=16 = 8 slot S + 8 slot O, mỗi slot 8 query M_Q). Nếu đảo thành kj ngoài, dvi trong để dùng lại P, thì phải giữ O cho tất cả dvi cùng lúc = DV_TILES × M_Q slot (LLaMA: 8×8 = 64 slot) — không vừa latch array. Nên họ chọn dvi ngoài và chấp nhận tính lại QK.

Cách sửa (giữ nguyên kích thước accumulator)

Cache P thay vì tính lại. P của một group chỉ là N_KV × M_Q giá trị FP4 ≈ KV_TILES × M_Q gói 72b:

  • LLaMA: 4 × 8 = 32 gói × 9 B ≈ 288 B — cực nhỏ, để được trong TCDM hoặc một buffer on-chip nhỏ.

Luồng mới:

Phase 1 (mỗi h, qi):  for kj: QK → softmax → LƯU P[kj]   (chạy 1 lần)
Phase 2 (mỗi dvi):    for kj: đọc P[kj] đã lưu, PV: O[dvi] += P[kj]·V[kj,dvi]
  • Vẫn chỉ cần 8 slot O (làm từng dvi một) → không đổi latch array.
  • Loại bỏ DV_TILES−1 lần QK + softmax + đọc lại K/Q thừa.
  • Cái giá: thêm nơi lưu P và cho PV đọc P từ đó (thay vì chỉ p_fifo depth-16). Có thể dùng chính snax_streamer_act_bcast để stream P từ TCDM trong pha PV.

Tóm lại: P không phụ thuộc dvi, nhưng thiết kế đang tính lại P cho mỗi dvi vì thiếu chỗ giữ O song song; cách tối ưu rẻ nhất là cache P (vài trăm byte) và tách QK/PV thành 2 pha.

Proposed P-cache algorithm:

Phase A (per h, qi): 
  for kj in 0..KV_TILES-1:
     QK: compute S = Q·K[kj]^T for M_Q queries (K_BLOCKS accumulations, 16 keys each) — same as now.
     softmax: drain 8 S slots → 8 P blocks
     store P[kj][m] (8 blocks) to a P buffer in TCDM (or on-chip)
  Also compute l (denominator) once per query — final after all kj. Store inv_l per query.

Phase B (per dvi in 0..DV_TILES-1):
  for kj in 0..KV_TILES-1:
     load P[kj][m] (8 blocks) from P buffer
     PV: O[m] += P[kj][m] · V[kj, dvi]  (M_Q beats)
  drain O slots → normalize with inv_l → FP16

This is exactly FlashAttention with K-loop outer producing P, then V-loop. But to fit O in 8 slots, we iterate dvi outer within phase B, recomputing PV but NOT QK. QK done once.

Key insight: In phase B, for each dvi we re-read P from the buffer. P is small. So QK is not recomputed.

But careful: the softmax online (running max) is computed in phase A across kj, so l and m are final at end of phase A. Good — we can store inv_l per query once. Then phase B uses it. This also removes the "l overwritten" serialization issue because l is computed once in phase A and read-only in phase B across all dvi. Actually even better: the background O-drain can fully overlap because l is stable.

Tradeoffs:
- Storage: need P buffer of KV_TILES × M_Q × 72b (for llama 32 × 9B = 288B) plus possibly per-query l. Could be in TCDM (cheap) or a dedicated on-chip SRAM/FIFO.
- If P stored in TCDM: need TCDM space + bandwidth to write P (during phase A) and read P (phase B, DV_TILES times). Reads = DV_TILES × KV_TILES × M_Q packets = for llama 8×4×8=256 packet reads per group. But QK avoided was 4096 beats; P reads 256 → still huge win. Actually P read is small compared to QK.
- Extra TCDM traffic vs QK savings: QK reads Q (M_Q × K_BLOCKS per kj) and K (16 lanes × K_BLOCKS per kj) per dvi. Avoided DV_TILES-1 times. P re-read each dvi is only KV_TILES×M_Q packets. Net bandwidth saving large.
- Control: one more phase (phase A/B), and a P store/load path. Could reuse write streamer (store P) and act streamer (read P) or a dedicated small buffer.

Alternative simpler variant that does NOT require re-reading P: reorder to kj-outer/dvi-inner but keep O for all dvi. Requires DV_TILES×M_Q O slots. For M_Q=8, DV_TILES=8 → 64 slots. Latch array would grow 8× (or use TCDM for O). This avoids both QK recompute and P re-read, but accumulates O[DV_TILES][M_Q] — storage heavy. Could spill O to TCDM between kj iterations (read-modify-write), which costs more bandwidth than caching P. So P-cache is the sweet spot.

Another alternative: keep dvi outer (current) but cache P and reuse — that's exactly proposed. Best.

Let me also discuss numerical equivalence: P-cache gives identical results because P identical; online softmax l computed once identically. So bit-exact preserved (just eliminate duplicate work). Actually current recomputes QK each dvi producing identical S → identical P → identical l → identical O. So proposed is numerically identical, still bit-exact. Good.

Algorithm A (current): dvi-outer, QK recomputed.
Algorithm B (proposed): QK-once + P cache, dvi-outer for PV.

Pros/cons table:
- QK compute: A = DV_TILES× redundant; B = 1×.
- PV compute: same both.
- Softmax: A = DV_TILES×; B = 1×.
- TCDM read traffic: A re-reads Q,K each dvi; B reads them once, plus P store+re-read.
- Storage: A minimal (transient p_fifo); B needs P buffer (small, ~hundreds B).
- Control complexity: A simpler (single loop nest); B adds phase split + P address management + mode switch for PV act source.
- l handling: A recomputes and must serialize O-drain (shared l); B computes once, read-only → better overlap.
- Latency/throughput: B much faster for DV_TILES>1.
- Energy: B less (fewer MACs, fewer TCDM reads).
- Risk: B changes datapath (PV must take P from buffer, not p_fifo) → more verification.
- Scalability with D_V: A cost grows linearly worse with DV_TILES; B constant QK.

Quantify: A total ≈ DV_TILES×(QK+softmax) + DV_TILES×PV_slice. B ≈ 1×(QK+softmax) + DV_TILES×PV_slice. Ratio B/A. For llama: QK=4096? Wait per group. So A=2304, B=512 per group → 4.5×. Yes.

Let me present the redesign concretely:

Tiling change:
- Split the attention into two distinct passes per (h, qi):
  Pass 1 "QK/Softmax pass" (over all KJ):
    for kj: launch act(Q), wt(K), mode=01; drain S(8 slots) → softmax; store P blocks to P-buffer[kj][m]; accumulate l across kj.
    After loop: compute final inv_l per query, store.
  Pass 2 "PV pass":
    for dvi:
      clear O slots (row_start)
      for kj: load P[kj][m], launch wt(V[kj,dvi]) mode=10; accumulate O.
      drain O(8 slots) → normalize with inv_l → write out.
- Addresses: P-buffer layout in TCDM, e.g., word = p_base + (kj*M_Q + m), each 72b. Need P base CSR + stride. Or on-chip.
- Datapath: in Pass 1, p_fifo output goes to P-store (write streamer or dedicated) instead of PV. In Pass 2, PV act source = P-buffer read (via act streamer or P FIFO preload).
- Core mode: same 01/10; only the P source routing changes.

Actually there's an even simpler implementation that avoids modifying core: keep using p_fifo but make it big enough to hold all P for the group (KV_TILES×M_Q = 32 blocks llama) and NOT pop between dvi — replay. But p_fifo currently consumed by PV and cleared. Could add a "P cache" SRAM that softmax writes and PV reads with a read pointer reset per dvi. Minimum change: enlarge p_fifo to KV_TILES*M_Q, and in Pass 2 loop dvi, reset p_fifo read pointer per dvi (don't clear between dvi). But p_fifo is a FIFO; replay needs a random-access read with reset pointer. Simpler to use a small SRAM/register file indexed [kj][m]. 

I'll mention both options: dedicated P-buffer (clean) or enlarge p_fifo + seek.

Also mention num_queries/l now computed in pass1: the l_accumulator is per query; pass2 just reads inv_l (already final) → the "background O drain" can start immediately after each dvi drain without waiting because l stable. Big simplification.

Also note: with P cached, K and Q only read once → allows Q in bank16 single stream; fine.

1. Thuật toán tiling mới

Loop nest hiện tại (A)

for h:
  for qi:
    for dvi:                       ← lặp DV_TILES lần
      for kj:
        QK (đọc Q,K)  → S(8 slot) → softmax → P
        PV (P × V[kj,dvi]) → O[dvi]
      drain O[dvi] → 1/l → FP16

Loop nest mới (B) — QK một lần, P cache

for h:
  for qi:
    # ---------- PASS 1: QK + Softmax, lưu P ----------
    for kj:
      QK (đọc Q,K) → S(8 slot) → softmax → P[kj][0..M_Q-1]
      ghi P[kj][*] vào P-buffer                    ← thay vì đẩy thẳng vào PV
      cộng dồn l (online max/denominator)
    chốt inv_l[0..M_Q-1] (đã final sau khi hết kj)

    # ---------- PASS 2: PV, tái dùng P ----------
    for dvi:
      clear O slots
      for kj:
        đọc P[kj][*] từ buffer                     ← không tính lại QK
        PV: O += P[kj][*] · V[kj,dvi]
      drain O → nhân inv_l (read-only) → FP16

Điểm mấu chốt: P không phụ thuộc dvi, nên dvi chỉ còn nằm trong pha PV. QK/softmax/l tính đúng 1 lần cho mỗi (h,qi).

2. Những gì phải sửa trong thiết kế

| Hạng mục | Hiện tại | Cần đổi |
|---|---|---|
| Loop nest | h→qi→dvi→kj | h→qi→{PASS1: kj}→{PASS2: dvi→kj} |
| FSM sequencer | QK_LAUNCH/RUN → SM_DRAIN → PV_LAUNCH/RUN → PV_DRAIN | thêm trạng thái ATTN_QK_PASS (kj loop) và ATTN_PV_PASS (dvi→kj loop); SM_DRAIN chỉ chạy trong PASS1 |
| Nơi chứa P | p_fifo depth 16, transient | P-buffer: KV_TILES × M_Q gói 72b (LLaMA = 4×8 = 32 gói ≈ 288 B) — đặt trong TCDM hoặc SRAM on-chip nhỏ |
| Địa chỉ P | không có | thêm CSR p_base, p_stride; layout word = p_base + kj*M_Q + m |
| Nguồn act của PV | p_fifo (sideband rescale) | đọc P từ P-buffer (có thể dùng lại snax_streamer_act_bcast để stream P như một stream 1 lane) |
| l / inv_l | tính lại mỗi dvi, dùng chung → phải serialize O-drain | tính 1 lần ở PASS1, PASS2 chỉ đọc → xóa được ràng buộc !nrm_busy |
| CSR descriptor | attnh, qtiles, dvtiles, kvtiles, k_blocks | giữ nguyên + thêm p_base/p_stride; dv_tiles chuyển vào vòng trong PASS2 |

Về datapath core thì không cần đổi công thức: mode 01 (QK) và mode 10 (P·V) giữ nguyên; chỉ đổi routing — PASS1 lấy output softmax ghi ra P-buffer, PASS2 nạp P từ buffer làm act_broadcast. Nhờ vậy kết quả vẫn bit-exact y hệt (P, l, O đều giống; chỉ bỏ phép tính lặp).

Biến thể đơn giản hơn nếu ngại sửa datapath: phóng to p_fifo thành KV_TILES×M_Q và cho PV " tua lại" (reset read-pointer mỗi dvi, không clear giữa các dvi). Ít xâm lấn hơn nhưng cần sửa p_fifo thành replayable buffer.

| P traffic thêm | 0 | ghi 32 + đọc 256 gói | +288 gói (nhỏ) |
| Tổng compute | 2304 | 512 | ≈4.5× nhanh hơn |

| Loop order PASS2 | P đọc mấy lần | O cần bao nhiêu slot |
|---|---|---|
| dvi-outer, kj-inner for dvi { for kj { đọc P[kj]; PV } } | đọc lại P mỗi dvi | M_Q slot (dùng lại cho từng dvi) + S |
| kj-outer, dvi-inner for kj { for dvi { PV dùng P[kj] } } | đọc P[kj] 1 lần, tái dùng cho mọi dvi | MQ × DVTILES slot + S |

Câu bạn trích mô tả kiểu thứ 2 (reuse P[kj] ngay trong vòng kj, không đọc lại). Chỉ khi đó mới cần 64 O slot cho M_Q=8, DV_TILES=8. Đó là lý do nó viết "8×8=64 slot + 8 S".

Nhưng phương án tôi đề xuất trước (PASS2 dvi-outer, kj-inner) không cần 64 slot — vẫn chỉ 8 O slot, vì xử lý xong một dvi thì drain rồi tái dùng slot cho dvi kế. Cái giá là đọc lại P từ buffer DV_TILES lần (rất nhỏ: ~288 B/lần).

⇒ Phát biểu "replay P thì phải 64 slot" không đúng như một điều kiện bắt buộc; nó chỉ đúng nếu chọn kiểu kj-outer (đọc P 1 lần). Nếu chọn kiểu dvi-outer + đọc lại P thì 16 slot (8S+8O) là đủ.

Ý 2: "pedefines.svh có sẵn macro ACCDEPTH_64/128" — đúng là có, nhưng không phải "cắm vào là chạy"

Đúng phần macro: pe_defines.svh:4-13 thật sự có

`ifdef ACC_DEPTH_128 → ACC_DEPTH_SYN 128
`elsif ACC_DEPTH_64  → ACC_DEPTH_SYN 64
`else                → ACC_DEPTH_SYN 4

Nhưng chưa đủ để mở rộng O, vì:

  1. snax_llm_top_clean không dùng macro này — nó có parameter ACC_DEPTH=16 và truyền .ACC_DEPTH_P(ACC_DEPTH). Macro chỉ là default cho snax_llm_top/shell (bản stub). Muốn 64 phải override param của top_clean.
  2. Độ rộng index bị hard-code 4 bit ở cả sequencer lẫn top:

- snax_llm_sequencer: output logic [3:0] tile_drain_idx_o, lane_acc_idx_o, cnt_dr_q 4 bit.
- snax_llm_top_clean: logic [3:0] tile_drain_idx, lane_acc_idx.
16 slot ⇒ 4 bit. Lên 64 phải thành 6 bit ở toàn bộ chuỗi.

  1. Cách chia vùng S/O hard-code 8:8, không tự scale:

- Sequencer ghi S slot = {1'b1, cnt_m_q[2:0]} (8..15), O slot = {1'b0, cnt_m_q[2:0]} (0..7).
- Core giải mã vùng bằng bit cao: drain_is_o_q <= ~tile_drain_idx_i[SLOT_AW-1].
Nếu ACCDEPTH=64 (SLOTAW=6), bit cao chia 32/32; giá trị {1'b1, c[2:0]}=8..15 rơi vào nửa thấp → bị hiểu là O. Tức là mapping S/O phải viết lại, không chỉ đổi macro.

  1. Diện tích/timing: latch_array DEPTH × TOTAL_W với TOTAL_W=16×32=512b. 64 slot = 32 Kb, 128 slot = 64 Kb latch + ICG; drain vẫn 1 slot/cycle nên không tự nhanh hơn.

⇒ "Đã có macro" = đúng, nhưng "mở rộng bộ tích lũy" thực tế cần sửa độ rộng index + encoding vùng S/O + tham số top cộng với diện tích, không phải bật define là xong.

Ý 3: "Mỗi dvi dùng chung sideband rescvalid/rescq/resc_r của kj đó để rescale O[dvi,q]" — ĐÚNG

Đúng, vì running max m và l chỉ phụ thuộc kj (và query), không phụ thuộc dvi:

  • softmax_requantizer sinh resc_* = 2^(m_old − m_new) khi blk_max > m_curr, và p_blk_out/csum cho block.
  • Trong PV, acc_rescale_req = (mode==10) && compute_fire && !p_fifo_empty && p_fifo_resc_valid, dùng p_fifo_resc_q/r. Sideband này đi kèm từng P block.
  • Với cùng kj, mọi dvi phải áp cùng resc_q/resc_r lên O[dvi,q] trước khi cộng P[kj]·V[kj,dvi]. Hệ quả thiết kế:

- Nếu cache P cho replay thì P-buffer phải lưu kèm sideband {resc_valid, resc_q, resc_r} (đúng như p_fifo đang lưu: P_FIFO_W = PKT_W + 12), nếu không PV ở PASS2 không rescale được.
- Điều kiện đúng: các beat O[dvi,q] của cùng kj phải được cộng trước khi sang kj kế tiếp (đúng với cả 2 kiểu loop order ở trên).
- Ở kiểu kj-outer/dvi-inner, rescale áp cho từng slot O[dvi,m] khi beat của nó chạy — vẫn nhất quán vì mọi dvi dùng chung một resc của kj.

Nếu bạn muốn theo kiểu kj-outer (đọc P 1 lần) thì mới cần mở ACC_DEPTH, và khi đó phải: (a) override ACC_DEPTH≥128, (b) nới index lên $clog2(ACC_DEPTH) ở sequencer/top, (c) định nghĩa lại encoding slot {dvi, query} thay cho {1'b1, m} và cập nhật drain_is_o_q + tile_drain_idx.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run.sh - build + run SNAX LLM top_clean testbenches with FST waveform dump
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TBDIR="$ROOT/tb/tb"          # python generators
SIMDIR="$ROOT/tb/sim"        # TB reads sim_snax_llm_top_*/hex here
FLDIR="$ROOT/filelists"
OUT="$ROOT/sim_out"
JOBS="$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 4)"

usage(){
  cat <<EOF
Usage: ./run.sh [target] [options] [-- <sim plusargs>]

  target: all | clean | gemm | llama   (default: all)

Options:
  --no-gen        Skip regenerating stimulus/golden (use existing tb/sim data)
  --no-build      Reuse existing Verilator build (skip rebuild)
  --no-trace      Run without FST waveform (much faster)
  --deep          Dump full TB hierarchy (+WAVE_DEEP), default dumps DUT only
  -j N            Verilator/g++ build parallelism (default: $JOBS)
  -h, --help      This help

Examples:
  ./run.sh clean                  # build + run with FST of the DUT
  ./run.sh gemm --deep            # full-hierarchy FST
  ./run.sh llama --no-gen          # reuse existing stimulus
  ./run.sh clean -- +NO_WAVE       # run without waves (fast)
EOF
}

TARGET="all"; DO_GEN=1; DO_BUILD=1; DO_TRACE=1; DEEP=0; SIM_PLUS=()
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    all|clean|gemm|llama) TARGET="$1"; shift;;
    --no-gen)   DO_GEN=0; shift;;
    --no-build) DO_BUILD=0; shift;;
    --no-trace) DO_TRACE=0; shift;;
    --deep)     DEEP=1; shift;;
    -j) JOBS="$2"; shift 2;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0;;
    --) shift; SIM_PLUS+=("$@"); break;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; usage; exit 1;;
  esac
done

mkdir -p "$OUT/build" "$OUT/waves" "$OUT/logs"

gen_one(){
  case "$1" in
    clean) python3 generate_snax_llm_top_clean_data.py;;
    gemm)  python3 generate_snax_llm_top_gemm_data.py;;
    llama) python3 generate_snax_llm_top_llama_data.py;;
  esac
}

run_one(){
  local name="$1"; local top="tb_snax_llm_top_$name"
  local bdir="$OUT/build/$name"
  local wave="$OUT/waves/$top.fst"
  local log="$OUT/logs/$top.log"

  if [[ "$DO_BUILD" == 1 ]]; then
    echo ">>> [build] $top"
    mkdir -p "$bdir"
    ( cd "$ROOT" && verilator --binary --timing -j "$JOBS" -Wno-fatal \
        --trace-fst -DFST_TRACE --top-module "$top" \
        -f "$FLDIR/tb_$name.f" \
        --Mdir "$bdir" -o "sim_$name" ) 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/logs/build_$name.log" | tail -n 3
  fi

  local args=()
  [[ "$DO_TRACE" == 1 ]] && args+=(--trace)
  [[ "$DEEP" == 1 ]] && args+=(+WAVE_DEEP)
  [[ ${#SIM_PLUS[@]} -gt 0 ]] && args+=("${SIM_PLUS[@]}")

  echo ">>> [run] $top ${args[*]:-}"
  ( cd "$SIMDIR" && "$bdir/sim_$name" "${args[@]}" ) 2>&1 | tee "$log"
  local rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

  if [[ -f "$SIMDIR/$top.fst" ]]; then
    mv "$SIMDIR/$top.fst" "$wave"
    echo ">>> waveform: $wave ($(du -h "$wave" | cut -f1))"
  fi
  echo ">>> result: $top rc=$rc  (log: $log)"
  return $rc
}

TARGETS=()
case "$TARGET" in
  all) TARGETS=(clean gemm llama);;
  *) TARGETS=("$TARGET");;
esac

if [[ "$DO_GEN" == 1 ]]; then
  echo ">>> generating stimulus/golden"
  ( cd "$TBDIR" && for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do gen_one "$t"; done )
fi

fail=0
for t in "${TARGETS[@]}"; do
  run_one "$t" || fail=1
done
exit $fail
```

They ask: why during drain is tile_drain_req interspersed with idle cycles in the middle (gaps between pulses)?

Looking at the waveform: tile_drain_req has pulses separated by idle cycles. tile_drain_acc_idx changes between pulses (0, then ?, 0, ...). lane_valid_in is 0 during drain.

This is the GEMM drain path in the sequencer: ST_GEMM_DRAIN → pulses tile_drain_req for one acc slot, then ST_GEMM_DRAIN_WAIT waits for core_fp16_valid to appear then be consumed, then advances to next beat (cnt_gbeat), back to ST_GEMM_DRAIN. That's why pulses are separated: the FSM waits for the FP16 output to be produced and consumed by the write-out streamer before requesting the next drain slot. This is the output backpressure / single hold register issue I mentioned earlier (5 cyc/slot).

So the "idle cycles in between" are ST_GEMM_DRAIN_WAIT: waiting for `core_fp16_valid_i` to assert (normalizer latency 2), then waiting for it to deassert (consumed by write-out streamer), and also `core_out_fifo_ready_i` gating. Each drain is paced by the consumer.

Let me confirm from the sequencer code:

ST_GEMM_DRAIN:
```
if (core_out_fifo_ready_i) begin
    tile_drain_req_o      = 1'b1;
    tile_drain_idx_o      = cnt_gbeat_q;
    tile_clear_on_drain_o = 1'b1;
    gemm_drain_seen_d     = 1'b0;
    state_d               = ST_GEMM_DRAIN_WAIT;

```
ST_GEMM_DRAIN_WAIT:
```
if (core_fp16_valid_i) gemm_drain_seen_d = 1'b1;

    if (last_gbeat) begin ... next launch or wait_write_out end
    else state_d = ST_GEMM_DRAIN;   // next slot
end
```
So between drain pulses: DRAIN (1 cycle) → DRAIN_WAIT (wait until core_fp16_valid seen then gone) → DRAIN. The wait is exactly the output handshake: normalizer produces vec_valid (2 cycles after drain), then write-out consumes it (FP16 path writes 4 words to same bank, ~4-5 cycles). So gap = latency + write-out time.

Also the `tile_drain_acc_idx` shows changing values / 0 during wait because cnt_gbeat advances only after handshake; during DRAIN_WAIT the index holds previous? Actually idx_o is driven combinationally = cnt_gbeat_q in DRAIN. In WAIT it defaults to 0 (the default assignment `tile_drain_idx_o = 4'd0;`), hence shows 0/xx during wait. And `tile_drain_req` pulses are the actual drain requests; the gaps are DRAIN_WAIT because the core's output (a 256b FP16 vector) must be consumed by the write-out streamer before the next accumulator slot can be drained — there's only a single output hold register, and FP16 write is serialized to the same bank.

Also note `core_out_fifo_ready_i` — in top, core_out_fifo_ready_o = 1'b1 (stub), so that gate always passes; the real pacing is DRAIN_WAIT.

So the answer: it's not "idle" in the sense of wasted by design—it's the intentional handshake pacing in ST_GEMM_DRAIN_WAIT: one drain pulse per accumulator slot, then wait for the drained vector to be normalized (2-cycle latency), presented on core_fp16_valid, and accepted/consumed by the write-out streamer before issuing the next drain. Because there is only one output hold register and the FP16 write-out serializes 4 words to the same bank (~4–5 cycles), each drain slot is spaced out.

ST_GEMM_DRAIN:                       // 1 chu kỳ: phát đúng 1 xung drain

Nên dãy thực tế là: DRAIN (1 cyc) → DRAIN_WAIT (vài cyc) → DRAIN → … Mỗi xung ứng với 1 slot, khoảng lặng là thời gian chờ bắt tay ngõ ra.

Vì sao phải chờ lâu như vậy

Chuỗi phụ thuộc cho một slot (đúng như đã đo ở phần review):

  1. tile_drain_req → matmul engine đọc slot, đăng ký raw_drained (1 cyc).
  2. final_normalizer có latency 2 cyc → mới có core_fp16_valid.
  3. core chỉ có 1 output hold register; vector phải được write-out streamer nhận (core_fp16_ready).
  4. Write-out FP16 ghi 4 word vào cùng bank 17 (line_stride=0x200), tuần tự 1 word/cyc → ~4 cyc nữa.
  5. Khi core_fp16_valid xuống (tiêu thụ xong), FSM mới cho phép drain slot kế.

Tổng cộng ≈ 5 cyc/slot ⇒ các xung drain cách nhau ~5 cyc. Đây chính là nút thắt ② (đường ra bị tuần tự hoá) đã nêu.

Giải thích các tín hiệu khác trong hình

  • lane_valid_in = 0000: đúng, GEMM đã tính xong, đang ở pha drain nên không có beat compute.
  • lane_acc_idx = 0 (và đoạn đỏ/X): trong DRAIN_WAIT tín hiệu này lấy giá trị mặc định 0 của khối comb (không mang nghĩa slot), nên thấy 0/X giữa các xung.
  • tile_drain_acc_idx: chỉ đúng giá trị slot (5, rồi slot kế…) trong đúng 1 chu kỳ DRAIN; ngoài ra về default 0.
  • nrm_state_q = NRM_IDLE: đúng — đây là engine drain nền cho attention, không dùng trong GEMM (GEMM drain nằm trên đường chính).
  • tile_clear_on_drain = 1: mask xoá slot sau khi xả (để slot tái dùng sạch cho tile sau).

Bạn sẽ thấy: xung tile_drain_req → +2 cyc core_fp16_valid bật → write-out chạy 4 word → core_fp16_valid tắt → xung drain kế. Khoảng lặng chính là đoạn này.

Ý nghĩa tối ưu

Trong chế độ GEMM, quá trình drain nằm ngay trên đường tới hạn (không có pha QK nền để che như attention), nên mỗi slot tốn ~5 cyc. Hai cách giảm:

  • Thêm output FIFO (8 entry) giữa normalizer và write-out để drain các slot liên tiếp 1 cyc/slot, write-out tự rút dần.
  • Stripe 4 word FP16 ra 4 bank khác nhau để ghi song song thay vì 4 cyc cùng bank 17.

Khi đó các khoảng lặng giữa tile_drain_req sẽ thu về ~1 cyc/slot, GEMM drain nhanh hơn đáng kể.

nếu bạn thêm 1 FIFO ở trong module snax_streamer_write_out thì sẽ giảm thậm chí triệt tiêu được những idle cycle ở giữa đúng không ?
Thinking
The user asks: if we add a FIFO inside snax_streamer_write_out, would it reduce/eliminate the idle cycles between drains?

I need to analyze carefully whether that's true. The key insight: the bottleneck is write-out writing 4 words serially to the same bank. An input FIFO at the write-out input would decouple the core from the write-out: the core could push vectors faster into the FIFO, and the write-out drains them. But the throughput of the write-out is still limited by 4 words/slot to the same bank = 4 cycles per vector. So a FIFO can absorb bursts but steady-state throughput is still 4 cycles/vector unless the write-out can output words faster.

So:
- FIFO absorbs transient bursts → removes per-slot handshake stalls → the core drain could go 1 cyc/slot until FIFO fills. But steady-state: the write-out still must write 4 words/vector at 1 word/cycle to the same bank → 4 cyc/vector. So the *average* rate of drain can't exceed 1 vector / 4 cycles if all vectors go to bank17 same bank.
- However, the drain period is currently 7. With a FIFO, the core can drain 1 cyc/slot and the write-out consumes at 4 cyc/vector. Over a tile of 16 slots: core pushes 16 in 16 cycles into FIFO (if depth ≥ 16?), write-out needs 16×4 = 64 cycles to drain. So the total time is still bounded by 64 cycles for 16 vectors = 4 cyc/vector average. The idle moves from "between drain pulses" to "FIFO full backpressure" or to "end of tile when waiting for FIFO to drain". So the idle cycles don't vanish; they're amortized/relocated, unless the write-out bandwidth improves.
- For a *single* tile's drain (16 slots), current: 16×7 = 112 cycles. With FIFO depth enough: core drains 16 in ~16+2 cycles, but then must wait for FIFO to empty before finishing? The FSM's done condition ST_WAIT_WRITE_OUT waits wo_done (write-out finished writing all). So total still ≥ 16×4=64 cycles for write-out, plus fill. So improvement from 112 → ~64-70. That's a real ~1.6× speedup, but "eliminate idle" no.
- To truly eliminate, need to increase write-out throughput: bank striping (4 words to 4 banks, 1 cyc/vector) or wider bank/write port.

Also there's the 2-cycle drain latency (matmul register + valid) and 1-cycle accept — a FIFO at write-out input doesn't remove the 2-cycle latency but the core can pipeline drains back-to-back (drain slot N+1 while slot N's vector is in flight) because the accumulator has 2 read ports (one for drain, one RMW), and drain_req can pulse every cycle. Actually can it? The drain path in vsq_matmul_engine: tile_drain_req → drain_req_q1 → core_vec_valid. If tile_drain_req pulses every cycle, the drain register updates every cycle, and core_vec_valid = drain_req_q1 every cycle → one vector per cycle (pipelined). But the output hold register is single-entry and `out_vec_fp16_valid = src_valid | hold`. If src_valid every cycle and ready (FIFO) high, it can accept 1/cycle. So with a FIFO that's always ready (until full), the core can indeed drain 1 slot/cycle. Good. So the burst is possible.

But the sequencer ST_GEMM_DRAIN gates on `core_out_fifo_ready_i` = core_fp16_ready. If we add a FIFO inside write-out and expose its "ready" (FIFO not full) as core_out_fp16_ready_o, then the sequencer can pulse drain every cycle until FIFO fills. So the per-slot spacing reduces to 1 cycle (+ latency pipelining). Great, that removes the 7→~1 for the burst.

So the answer: Yes, a FIFO *at the input of write-out, with its "not-full" as ready*, will eliminate the inter-drain idle during the burst — the core can drain back-to-back. BUT it does NOT increase the write-out's raw write throughput (4 words/vector to one bank). So:
- Short term (one tile of 16 vectors): faster (burst drain), then the tile completion waits for the FIFO to drain at 4 cyc/vector. Total time bounded by max(core drain burst, write-out write time) = ~64 cycles instead of 112. So ~1.7× for the drain phase.

FIFO sửa được gì và không sửa được gì

Nhìn lại 7 cycle/slot hiện tại:

1 (pulse) + 1 (matmul reg) + 1 (valid+accept) + 4 (write 4 word, 1 word/cyc)

Trong đó 4 cycle ghi là sàn cứng: 1 vector FP16 = 256b = 4 word 72b, mà write-out chỉ có 1 master port 72b (master 19) → 4 chu kỳ bất kể FIFO.

FIFO đặt ở input write-out (lưu cả vector 256b), với ready = !fifo_full, sẽ:

  • Gỡ ràng buộc bắt tay: core đẩy được vector mỗi chu kỳ, nên 2 cycle latency + 1 accept được pipelining, core drain liên tiếp thay vì chờ.
  • Khoảng cách drain tụt từ 7 → ~4 cycle/slot (đúng bằng sàn ghi TCDM).
  • Nhưng không làm 4-word-write nhanh hơn → throughput trung bình vẫn ≤ 1 vector / 4 cycle.

Nếu FSM vẫn đợi wo_done cuối tile (ST_WAIT_WRITE_OUT), các bubble chỉ dồn về cuối burst chứ không mất. Ví dụ tile GEMM 16 slot:

| Phương án | Drain 16 slot | Ghi chú |
|---|---|---|
| Hiện tại | 16 × 7 = 112 cyc | bubble xen giữa |
| FIFO, vẫn đợi flush cuối tile | ~18 (burst) + 64 (flush 16×4) ≈ 66–70 cyc | nhanh ~1.6×, bubble về đuôi |
| FIFO + overlap với compute tile kế | ẩn hoàn toàn | idle ≈ 0 nếu compute ≥ 64 cyc |

Hai cách để "triệt tiêu" thật sự

① Overlap (hiệu quả nhất, giống engine nrm của attention):
Cho write-out tự rút FIFO chạy nền trong khi FSM sang tile compute kế. Vì:

  • compute dùng master 2 (act) + 3..18 (wt) đọc bank 0..16,
  • write-out dùng master 19 ghi bank 17,

→ crossbar cho chạy song song, không đụng bank. Khi đó 4 cyc/vector ghi bị che sau compute → không còn idle.
Cần sửa FSM: ST_GEMM_DRAIN không chờ flush; chỉ chờ wo_done ở cuối job.

② Tăng băng thông cổng ra (nếu muốn giảm cả sàn):

  • Mở rộng port write-out thành 288b (4×72b) hoặc thêm 3 master port ghi song song 4 word ra 4 bank khác nhau → 1 cyc/vector. (Lưu ý: chỉ stripe bank mà vẫn 1 master port thì không nhanh hơn, vì vẫn serialize 1 word/cyc — điều này tôi nói chưa chuẩn ở phần trước.)
  • Hoặc ghi FP4 72b (1 word/vector) cho đường trung gian, chỉ xuất FP16 khi CPU cần.

Về kết nối / độ sâu FIFO

  • core_out_fp16_ready_o của write-out nên = !fifo_full. Hiện sequencer đã nối core_out_fifo_ready_i ← core_fp16_ready (tức ready write-out), nên chỉ cần thay ready cũ !fp16_active_q bằng !fifo_full là sequencer tự drain back-to-back, không cần sửa FSM.
  • Độ sâu: nếu chỉ cần hấp thụ 1 burst của tile → depth ≥ số vector/tile (GEMM 16 → 16 entry × 256b = 512 B, rẻ). Nếu có overlap, FIFO nhỏ vài entry cũng đủ vì tốc độ sản xuất ≈ tiêu thụ trên mỗi tile.
  • Giữ hold-register hiện tại cũng được; FIFO đặt sau nó (hoặc thay luôn).

Kết luận

  • Có FIFO → giảm idle từ 7 → ~4 cyc/slot (do pipeline hoá 2 cyc latency + accept), đúng như bạn nghĩ.
  • Chưa triệt tiêu vì sàn 4-word-write qua 1 port 72b vẫn còn; nếu đợi flush cuối tile thì chỉ dồn bubble về đuôi.
  • Triệt tiêu khi FIFO + cho write-out chạy nền song song compute (khuyến nghị), hoặc thêm multi-port / port rộng 288b để hạ sàn xuống 1 cyc/vector.

Nếu bạn muốn, tôi có thể sửa snax_streamer_write_out thêm input FIFO (tham số FIFO_DEPTH), đổi core_out_fp16_ready_o = !full, rồi đo lại period trên TB gemm để xác nhận 7 → 4.

2: // Module: snax_streamer_write_out
3: // Description: Linear FP4 / FP16 output writer plus V FP4 batch writer.

5: // Modes:
6: //   2'd0 : FP4 linear   - one 72b packet per vector
7: //   2'd1 : FP16 linear  - one 256b FP16 vector -> 4 x 72b words
8: //   2'd2 : V FP4 batch  - cfg_num_vectors channel packets per batch
9: //
10: // V mode address:
11: //   addr = cfg_base_addr_i + batch * cfg_batch_stride_i
12: //                        + channel * cfg_line_stride_i
13: //   Typical V layout: cfg_num_vectors=16, cfg_line_stride=16,
14: //                     cfg_batch_stride=0x200.
15: // =============================================================================
16: `timescale 1ns/1ps

18: module snax_streamer_write_out #(
19:     parameter int unsigned DATA_WIDTH = 72,
20:     parameter int unsigned ADDR_WIDTH = 32,
21:     parameter int unsigned NUM_LANES  = 16,
22:     parameter int unsigned STRB_WIDTH = 9
23: )(

25:     input  logic                            rst_n,

31:     input  logic [1:0]                      cfg_mode_i,          // 0 FP4, 1 FP16, 2 V FP4
32:     input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]           cfg_base_addr_i,
33:     input  logic [31:0]                     cfg_num_vectors_i,   // packets per batch / linear vectors
34:     input  logic [31:0]                     cfg_line_stride_i,    // per packet / per FP16 word / per channel
35:     input  logic [31:0]                     cfg_num_batches_i,    // V mode batches
36:     input  logic [31:0]                     cfg_batch_stride_i,   // V mode batch stride
37: 
38:     input  logic [NUM_LANES*16-1:0]         core_out_fp16_data_i,
39:     input  logic                            core_out_fp16_valid_i,

45: 
46:     output logic                            m_tcdm_req_valid_o,

54:     localparam logic [1:0] MODE_FP4  = 2'd0;
55:     localparam logic [1:0] MODE_FP16 = 2'd1;
56:     localparam logic [1:0] MODE_V    = 2'd2;
57: 
58:     typedef enum logic [1:0] {
59:         IDLE,
60:         WRITE_FP4,
61:         WRITE_FP16,
62:         WRITE_V
63:     } state_t;
64: 
65:     state_t state_q, state_d;
66: 
67:     logic [31:0]           vec_cnt_q,    vec_cnt_d;

69:     logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] write_addr_q, write_addr_d;

72:     logic [NUM_LANES*16-1:0] fp16_vec_q, fp16_vec_d;
73:     logic                  fp16_active_q, fp16_active_d;
74:     logic                  start_q;
75: 
76:     // Job descriptor, sampled once at start.  The producer is free to change
77:     // cfg_* afterwards (the sequencer only presents the descriptor during its
78:     // launch state), so the engine must not read these live.
79:     logic [1:0]            mode_q;
80:     logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] base_q;

91:     wire [1:0]            mode    = (state_q == IDLE) ? cfg_mode_i         : mode_q;
92:     wire [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] base    = (state_q == IDLE) ? cfg_base_addr_i    : base_q;
93:     wire [31:0]           nvec    = (state_q == IDLE) ? cfg_num_vectors_i  : nvec_q;
94:     wire [31:0]           lstride = (state_q == IDLE) ? cfg_line_stride_i  : lstride_q;
95:     wire [31:0]           nbatch  = (state_q == IDLE) ? cfg_num_batches_i  : nbatch_q;

98:     function automatic logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] pack_fp16_word(

102:         pack_fp16_word = {8'h00,
103:                           vec[(word*4 + 3)*16 +: 16],
104:                           vec[(word*4 + 2)*16 +: 16],

106:                           vec[(word*4 + 0)*16 +: 16]};
107:     endfunction

109:     always_comb begin
110:         state_d               = state_q;

114:         batch_base_d          = batch_base_q;
115:         word_cnt_d            = word_cnt_q;
116:         fp16_vec_d            = fp16_vec_q;

118:         done_irq_o            = 1'b0;

127: 
128:         case (state_q)
129:             IDLE: begin

135:                         vec_cnt_d     = '0;
136:                         batch_cnt_d   = '0;

138:                         batch_base_d  = base;
139:                         word_cnt_d    = '0;
140:                         fp16_active_d = 1'b0;
141:                         case (mode)
142:                             MODE_FP16: state_d = WRITE_FP16;
143:                             MODE_V:    state_d = WRITE_V;
144:                             default:   state_d = WRITE_FP4;
145:                         endcase
146:                     end
147:                 end
148:             end
149:             // -------------------------------------------------------------
150:             // Linear FP4: one 72b packet per vector
151:             // -------------------------------------------------------------
152:             WRITE_FP4: begin
153:                 core_out_fp4_ready_o = m_tcdm_req_ready_i;
154: 
155:                 if (core_out_fp4_valid_i) begin
156:                     m_tcdm_req_valid_o = 1'b1;
157:                     m_tcdm_req_wdata_o = core_out_fp4_data_i;
158: 
159:                     if (tcdm_fire) begin

166:                             state_d    = IDLE;
167:                         end
168:                     end
169:                 end
170:             end
171: 
172:             // -------------------------------------------------------------
173:             // Linear FP16: one 256b vector -> 4 x 72b words
174:             // -------------------------------------------------------------
175:             WRITE_FP16: begin
176:                 core_out_fp16_ready_o = !fp16_active_q;
177: 
178:                 if (!fp16_active_q) begin
179:                     if (core_out_fp16_valid_i) begin

193:                         end else begin
194:                             word_cnt_d    = '0;
195:                             fp16_active_d = 1'b0;
196: 
197:                             if (vec_cnt_q < nvec - 1'b1) begin
198:                                 vec_cnt_d = vec_cnt_q + 1'b1;
199:                             end else begin
200:                                 done_irq_o = 1'b1;
201:                                 state_d    = IDLE;
202:                             end
203:                         end
204:                     end
205:                 end
206:             end
207: 
208:             // -------------------------------------------------------------
209:             // V FP4 batch: cfg_num_vectors channel packets per batch
210:             // -------------------------------------------------------------

212:                 core_out_fp4_ready_o = m_tcdm_req_ready_i;

214:                 if (core_out_fp4_valid_i) begin

So to overlap next tile's compute with current tile's drain, you'd need double-buffered accumulators: 16 slots for current drain + 16 for next compute = 32 slots. ACC_DEPTH would need 32. The macro supports 64/128! So we can use ACC_DEPTH=32 (or 64) and ping-pong two banks of 16.
- Then the FSM can, after a tile finishes accumulating, start draining tile N (from bank A) while launching compute of tile N+1 into bank B. The background drain writes via write-out (already background). Actually the "drain" produces FP16 vectors pushed to write-out FIFO; the write-out writes TCDM in background. So the "drain" is cheap (Port B read + normalize) and can be interleaved with compute beats using the 2R1W latch array (Port A compute RMW, Port B drain) — exactly like attention! The latch array is 2-read-1-write: Port A RMW, Port B drain. So simultaneous compute + drain is supported by hardware.
- The FSM would need a background drain engine for GEMM analogous to `nrm` engine for attention: drain 16 slots of the finished tile while the main FSM proceeds to next tile's compute.

Now, the critical correctness concern: gating compute beat t on `t < gdr_idx` ensures drain issued slot t before compute beat t. But does it also prevent the compute from writing slot t before the drain READ? Drain issues slot t at cycle D_t (pulse). Compute beat t can fire at earliest cycle when gdr_idx > t, i.e., the cycle AFTER D_t (since gdr_idx increments at posedge after issuing). So A_t (lane_valid_in) ≥ D_t+1. Stage2 write at A_t+2 ≥ D_t+3. Drain read at D_t (Port B). So read well before write. Clear visible D_t+1 ≤ A_t+2. Good. Safe.

But wait: `gdr_idx_q` increments only when `core_out_fifo_ready_i`. And the drain pulse happens with idx=D_t. At the same posedge, idx<=idx+1. So when idx>t, slot t was issued. Compute beat t allowed when idx>t, i.e., starting the cycle after the pulse for slot t. Good.

Edge: when drain inactive (gdr_idx=16, active=0) → beat_ok = !active = 1. All allowed. Good.

Edge: first tile: active=0 → allowed. Good.

Edge: If drain finishes (active=0) but gdr_idx=16, beat_ok=1. Good.

Now, the gating also stalls the streamers: if we don't assert act_ready/wt_ready when beat_ok=0, the streamer holds. Good. But note: `gemm_compute_fire` now includes beat_ok, and in ST_GEMM_RUN only fires when beat_ok. act_ready/wt_ready set inside the `if (gemm_compute_fire)` block. Good.

But `gemm_compute_fire` is also used in the counter block; with gating included, counters advance only on actual gated fires. Good.

Now, potential deadlock: Suppose drain active, gdr_idx small, and compute beat 0 waits (beat_ok false because 0<0 false when idx=0). Drain needs core_out_fifo_ready_i to advance. FIFO is empty at tile start → ready=1 → drain advances. So no deadlock. Unless FIFO full from previous tile's backlog — but write-out drains during compute; by tile start likely empty. If not, drain waits, compute waits — but write-out continues popping → FIFO frees → drain advances. So progress. Good.

Now, another subtlety: The drain engine pulses tile_drain_req while the main FSM might be in ST_GEMM_LAUNCH (launching streamers) or ST_GEMM_RUN. The matmul drain reads Port B. During ST_GEMM_LAUNCH, lane_valid=0, so only drain. Fine. During ST_GEMM_RUN, lane_valid asserted for beats; Port A + Port B. Fine.

But the mode: In ST_GEMM_LAUNCH/RUN, cfg_mode_o=00. During drain in background, cfg_mode=00, drain_is_o_q etc. For GEMM, `norm_drain_req = raw_drained_valid && (mode10 || drain_is_o_q)`. drain_is_o_q is registered from `~tile_drain_idx_i[SLOT_AW-1]`. For ACC_DEPTH=16, SLOT_AW=4, bit3. Slots 0..7 → bit3=0 → drain_is_o_q=1 → norm_drain_req=1 (runs normalizer, unused). Slots 8..15 → 0 → norm not run. But the GEMM output uses gemm_vec (matmul's own norm), not final_normalizer. So fine. But note: final_normalizer running could produce vec_valid on norm_vec, but src selects gemm_vec in mode00. So ignored. OK.

Now, there's a concern about `drain_is_o_q` being registered from tile_drain_req and used same cycle? It's used in `sm_in_valid` and `norm_drain_req` in the next cycle. For GEMM mode sm not used. Fine.

With our gating, compute Stage2 slot (lane_acc_idx_q1) and drain idx differ by ~2 (drain ahead), so different. Good.

1. snax_streamer_write_out.sv (FIFO, đã làm trước đó)

2. snax_llm_sequencer.sv (overlap — mới)

  • Engine drain nền: gemm_drain_active_q + gdr_idx_q (0..15). Kích hoạt tại gemm_k_last_fire (= beat cuối K-block cuối). Mỗi chu kỳ phát tile_drain_req, idx=gdr_idx, clear=1, tăng dần tới 15; gate bởi core_out_fifo_ready_i để không tràn output.
  • Gate compute theo drain: gemm_beat_ok = !drain_active || (beat_idx < gdr_idx). Beat t của tile kế chỉ chạy khi slot t đã được drain+clear → nếu drain stall thì compute stall (an toàn).

The user shows a GEMM waveform: state_q alternates between ST_GEMM_.. (launch?) and ST_GEMM_RUN. lane_valid_in is ffff for a while, then 0000 for 2-3 cycles, then ffff again. They ask: why are there 2-3 idle cycles inserted in lane_valid, even though TCDM bandwidth for weight and activation is sufficient?

Looking at waveform: state_q shows "ST_GE..." (probably ST_GEMM_LAUNCH) then "ST_GEMM_RUN", repeating. lane_valid_in is ffff (16) for ~16 cycles, then 0000 for ~2-3 cycles, repeating. So every 16 beats there's a gap. And tile_drain appears at the far right starting.

So the gap occurs between K-blocks: after 16 beats (cnt_gbeat 0..15) of a K-block, the FSM goes ST_GEMM_RUN → ST_GEMM_LAUNCH (next K-block) → ST_GEMM_RUN. The LAUNCH state re-launches the act/wt streamers, and there's a pipeline fill latency before data is valid again → 2-3 idle cycles. That's the 2-3 idle between lane_valid bursts.

Let me verify: In GEMM, for each (gm,gn) tile, K_BLOCKS passes. Each K pass is ST_GEMM_LAUNCH then ST_GEMM_RUN for 16 beats. At last_gbeat && !last_gk → ST_GEMM_LAUNCH (next K block). The streamers need to be re-launched (act_start/wt_start), and their skid buffers start empty → a few cycles of pipeline fill (TCDM read latency ~?) before act_valid & wt_valid both high → 2-3 idle cycles.

So the gap is the **per-K-block streamer relaunch + pipeline fill**, NOT a bandwidth issue. The TCDM has bandwidth, but the streamer FSM restarts each K-block: ST_GEMM_LAUNCH asserts start, streamers go IDLE→RUN, issue first TCDM reads, responses come back after read latency (~2-3 cycles), skid fills, then valid. During that fill, lane_valid=0.

Also the FSM ST_GEMM_LAUNCH itself may take ≥1 cycle (it waits `core_can_pop && !act_busy && !wt_busy`; if streamers are done, launches same cycle, state→RUN). Then RUN waits for act_valid & all wt_valid (gemm_compute_fire) → the fill.

Why relaunch per K-block instead of streaming continuously? Because the act streamer's AGU is configured with act_k_blocks=1, k_stride=0, and the FSM relaunches for each K-block with a new base address (gemm_act_addr depends on cnt_gk). Similarly wt. So each K-block = separate launch → fill bubble.

The user asks: "Is the current RTL top enough to run the full computation of one LLM layer at prefill?"

This is a architecture/functional-coverage question. I need to assess whether snax_llm_top_clean can execute a full LLM layer in prefill mode, based on the RTL analysis I've done.

Let me think about what a full LLM layer (prefill) requires:
- Transformer layer: 
  1. RMSNorm (input)
  2. QKV projection (GEMM): X[M, d_model] × W_qkv[d_model, d_kv] 
  3. RoPE on Q,K
  4. Attention: QK^T softmax V (FlashAttention) per head, GQA
  5. Output projection (GEMM)
  6. Residual add
  7. RMSNorm
  8. FFN: gate/up projections (GEMM), SiLU/GELU (SwiGLU), down projection (GEMM)
  9. Residual add
- Prefill = process many tokens (M > 1) in parallel, no KV cache decode.

Now the RTL subsystem:
- Has GEMM engine (M tiles × N tiles × K blocks).
- Has FlashAttention (QK/PV) with softmax.
- Has CPU RV32I TCDM port for "RoPE, RMSNorm, SiLU" per comments.
- Has DMA master for DRAM<->TCDM.
- Everything at FP4 log-scale.

So does the top have the primitives? Let me assess what's actually supported vs missing:

1. **GEMM**: Yes, dense GEMM supported (tb_snax_llm_top_gemm proves M=32,N=32,K=64). Can do QKV projections, output proj, FFN projections. But precision is FP4 log-scale (weights/activations quantized to E2M1 with per-16 log scale). That's very low precision (4-bit). For a real LLM layer this is aggressive but "computes".

2. **Attention**: Yes, FlashAttention QK/PV with exp-free softmax, causal mask, online rescale. The clean/llama TBs prove it with H, N_Q, N_KV, D_K, D_V. So attention core works.

3. **RoPE, RMSNorm, SiLU/SwiGLU**: These are NOT hardware blocks in the RTL; they're expected to run on the **RV32I CPU** via the TCDM master port 1. The RTL just provides the TCDM access port and CSR. There is NO RMSNorm/RoPE/SiLU hardware. So "full layer" requires a CPU core (RV32I) that isn't part of this top (it's an external master interface). Actually the top takes `cpu_mem_req_*` and `cpu_csr_*` as inputs — it assumes an external CPU. So the subsystem itself is an accelerator; the CPU must be attached to do elementwise ops.

4. **Data types / precision**: Everything is FP4 (E2M1) with log-scale. Input FP16 from quantizer. The layer would need to quantize FP16→FP4 at boundaries. The log_quantizer does that. But there's no FP16/FP32 dense GEMM; only FP4. Also residual add (FP16) not in hardware → CPU.

5. **Multi-head / GQA**: The sequencer supports H heads, Q tiles, DV slices, KV tiles; but each head processed; attention head dim D_K must be multiple of 16. GQA (shared K/V across query groups) not explicitly; the loop nest is h→qi→dvi→kj. Possibly can map.

6. **KV cache / decode**: prefill only. The question is prefill, so okay. Though the design recomputes QK per dvi (inefficient but works).

7. **Full layer orchestration**: The sequencer supports ONE opcode per start: GEMM, FlashAttention, V transpose/quant, readback. To run a full layer you'd need the CPU/software to sequence multiple jobs (CSR-configured): norm→QKV GEMM→RoPE→attn→out proj→residual→norm→FFN GEMMs→... Each as separate accelerator jobs. There is no single "layer" descriptor/hardware that chains all. So "full layer" requires firmware orchestration via CSR + CPU elementwise kernels.

8. **Memory capacity**: TCDM 288KB (32 banks × 1024 × 72b = 288KB). For a prefill layer with real dimensions (e.g., LLaMA-7B d_model=4096, seq len 2048), weights are huge (billions of params), can't fit in TCDM; must stream via DMA from DRAM. The DMA ring buffer (4×16KB=64KB) prefetches tiles. The GEMM streams weight tiles. But the sequencer's DMA prefetch is credit-based for KV ring; for weight streaming it uses `cfg_enable_dma`. Does it actually stream arbitrary large weights? The DMA descriptor moves SLOT_SIZE_BYTES (16KB) per tile. The address computation uses fixed strides. So it can stream tiles, but capacity/bandwidth is limited. Still "can run" if orchestrated.

9. **Elementwise in FP4**: RMSNorm needs FP16/FP32 precision; the CPU would compute on FP16 data in TCDM (the write-out FP16 path exists so CPU can read/modify FP16). So RMSNorm on CPU reading FP16 from TCDM. But the CPU interface is 72-bit per access (9 bytes) — awkward for FP16. Hmm.

10. **Numerical correctness**: FP4 attention verified bit-exact vs golden model that shares the same quantized math. But is it "LLM-accurate"? Not a correctness question about RTL.

So the answer: The top provides the compute engine primitives (FP4 GEMM + FlashAttention + quantizer + TCDM + DMA + CPU port), enough to *exercise* all matmul/attention math of a prefill layer, but it is NOT a self-contained "one LLM layer" — you still need:
- A host CPU/RV32I to do RMSNorm, RoPE, SiLU/SwiGLU, residual adds (no hardware), and to orchestrate the sequence of jobs via CSR.
- Firmware sequencing multiple GEMM/attention jobs.
- Enough DRAM/weight streaming; TCDM only holds tiles (288KB).
- Precision is FP4 log-scale; layer boundaries need quantization; accuracy will be low.
- No KV-cache decode (prefill only fine).
- Multi-head/GQA and real dimensions constrained by tile sizes and address map.

Precision issue: The GEMM/attention are FP4 log-scale with specific quantization (quantize_block thresholds). The CPU elementwise for RMSNorm/RoPE/SiLU would operate on FP16 (post-GEMM output) then the next GEMM input must be re-quantized FP16→FP4 (uses log_quantizer). So the CPU needs to: read FP16 from TCDM, compute FP16 norm/rope/silu, write FP16 back, then invoke the quantizer path? Or the GEMM's activation streamer reads FP4 packets directly. So between FP16 elementwise and next GEMM, must quantize FP16→FP4 and store as packets in TCDM in the GEMM's expected layout. The quantizer hardware (log_quantizer) takes FP16 in and produces FP4 packet; but it's driven by the core output path, not by CPU directly. Could the CPU write FP16 then use the "readback requantize" path? Complex.

This reveals that the intended flow likely: GEMM output FP16 → CPU does norm/rope/silu in FP16 → write FP16 to TCDM → use a separate quantization job (readback FP4 requantize) to convert FP16→FP4 packets for the next GEMM. The RTL has "readback" opcode (rd_start) that reads FP16 from TCDM via read streamer and feeds quantizer→write streamer to write FP4 packets. So the sequence is supported! Good.

So a full layer flow per stage:
1. DMA load weights (FP4 packets already? or FP16 then quantize?) — weights likely pre-quantized to FP4 offline and stored in DRAM, DMA loads packets.
2. Activations: FP16 input quantized to FP4 (offline or via readback requant).
3. GEMM → FP16 output bank17.
4. CPU reads FP16, does RoPE/norm/silu, writes FP16.
5. Requantize job (readback) FP16→FP4 packets into the layout GEMM/attention expects.
6. Attention job → FP16 output.
7. etc.

So the hardware does support the flow via opcodes: GEMM, V transpose, readback-requant, attention. The CPU/DMA glue is what's needed.

Implement real_to_fp16 reasonably:
```
function automatic logic [15:0] real_to_fp16(input real v);
  logic s; real a, norm; int expn; logic [4:0] e; logic [9:0] mant; real frac;
  if (v == 0.0) return 16'h0000;
  s = (v < 0.0); a = s ? -v : v;
  expn = 0;
  // normalize to [1,2)
  while (a >= 2.0) begin a = a/2.0; expn++; end
  while (a < 1.0)  begin a = a*2.0; expn--; end
  // exponent bias 15
  if (expn + 15 <= 0) return {s, 15'b0, 10'b0}; // subnormal/zero (approx)
  if (expn + 15 >= 31) return {s, 5'b11111, 10'b0};
  e = expn + 15;
  frac = a - 1.0;
  mant = $rtoi(frac * 1024.0 + 0.5);
  if (mant >= 1024) begin mant = 0; e = e + 1; end
  return {s, e, mant[9:0]};
endfunction
```
Good enough for tolerance.

```
task automatic cpu_rmsnorm1(input logic [31:0] a, input real g0,g1,g2,g3);
  logic [71:0] w; real x[0:3]; real ss, rms, inv; logic [15:0] f;
  cpu_mem_read(a,w);
  for(int k=0;k<4;k++) x[k]=fp16_to_real(w[k*16+:16]);
  ss=0; for(int k=0;k<4;k++) ss+=x[k]*x[k];
  rms=$sqrt(ss/4.0); inv=(rms==0.0)?0.0:1.0/rms;
  w=72'd0;
  x[0]=x[0]*inv*g0; x[1]=x[1]*inv*g1; x[2]=x[2]*inv*g2; x[3]=x[3]*inv*g3;
  w[15:0]=real_to_fp16(x[0]); w[31:16]=real_to_fp16(x[1]); w[47:32]=real_to_fp16(x[2]); w[63:48]=real_to_fp16(x[3]);
  cpu_mem_write(a,w);
endtask
```

```
def mu_of(h):
    E=(h>>10)&0x1F; M=h&0x3FF
    if E==0: return 0
    if E==31: return 247
    return ((E<<3)|(M>>7))&0xFF
def mag_of(d):
    TH=[(2,7),(6,6),(10,5),(14,4),(18,3),(24,2),(36,1)]
    for t,m in TH:
        if d<=t: return m
```

Answer: No. The `cpu_quantize16` task I wrote is a **software model in the testbench**, replicating the same arithmetic as the RTL `log_quantizer`/`slq_encoder`. It does NOT use the hardware log-quantizer block. It reads FP16 words from TCDM via the CPU master port and computes the packet in SV tasks, then writes the packet back to TCDM. The HW log_quantizer is a separate datapath (in top_clean: `u_log_quantizer`, driven by `quant_fp16_in`/`in_valid` from the mux fed by core/transpose/readback), and it's commanded by the readback/requant job — not accessible to the CPU directly.

So: the CPU quantizer is a duplicate software implementation for the layer orchestration/golden; it matches the HW semantics bit-exactly (verified), but it's not the HW block. If we wanted to use the HW quantizer for the layer, we'd need to drive it through the readback-requant path: CPU writes FP16, then start a readback job (opcode 11) with quant_src_sel=readback, which reads FP16 via master20 → quantizer → write-out writes FP4 packets. That exercises the actual HW.

The user wants me to add the HW readback-requant job to exercise the actual hardware log-quantizer in the layer TB.

Let me understand the readback-requant path in top_clean:
- The sequencer opcode 11 (`ST_RD_LAUNCH/RUN`) does readback+requantize.
- Signals: `rd_start`, `rd_base`, `rd_num_vectors`, `rd_line_stride`.
- Read streamer `snax_stream_read_fp16` (master 20) reads 4×72b words per 256b FP16 vector, assembles, outputs `rd_fp16_data`/`rd_fp16_valid`.
- The quantizer mux: `src_rd_sel = !v_active && (rd_busy || cfg_quant_src_sel==2'b10)`. So when rd_busy, selects readback source; `quant_fp16_in=rd_fp16_data; quant_in_valid=rd_fp16_valid && quant_accept`.
- Quantizer → `wo_fp4_data`/`wo_fp4_valid` → write-out FP4 (master19).
- The write-out must be started with mode FP4 and a base/count to write packets.

In top_clean, `wo_job_start = wo_start | v_start | rd_start`. So starting rd_start also starts write-out. The sequencer ST_RD_LAUNCH sets:
```
cfg_enable_slq=1;
rd_start_o=1;
wo_start_o=1;
wo_mode_o=2'd0; // FP4 linear
wo_base_o = cfg_rd_out_base_i;
wo_num_vectors_o = cfg_rd_num_vectors_i;
wo_line_stride_o = cfg_rd_line_stride_i;
```
Then ST_RD_RUN until rd_done && !wo_busy.

So the HW readback-requant job:
- Reads `rd_num_vectors` FP16 vectors from `rd_base` (each vector = 4 words at `rd_base + (i*4 + w)*rd_line_stride`), assembles 256b, quantizes → 72b packet, writes packet to `rd_out_base + i*wo_line_stride`.

Wait, the write-out in FP4 mode writes one packet per vector; `wo_line_stride` is the address step per packet. So we configure `rd_num_vectors`, `rd_line_stride` (word step for FP16 words), `wo_base`=out, `wo_line_stride`=packet step.
